newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - TATA SHOWS TASTE FOR INDIAN.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - TATA SHOWS TASTE FOR INDIAN.

text.p: Tata Electric Co Ltd's US$300 million two-tranche 144a this week shows the depth of appetite for quality Indian debt, bankers said.
The 10-year tranche was issued at 99.611 to yield 160 basis points over U.S. treasuries.
Term lender the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp Of India also paid 160 basis points over Treasuries at the start of the month for a 10-year bond.
"There's more demand than...supply," said one banker, who had earlier thought Tata Electric's paper could go at 140 to 155 basis points over treasuries.
Tata Electric's spread was narrower than Tata Engineering & Locomotive Co's US$200 million issue in July, which was at 168 basis points over treasuries.
Tata Electric's 20-year tranche was priced at 99.354 to yield 193 basis points over the 30-year treasury. The Tata Electric issue is rated BB+ by Standard & Poor's.
Bankers said rarity value was helping Indian debt sell, as well as a fall in primary debt issues from elsewhere in Asia.
"There's been a drought in these (Indian) issues, which makes them very attractive to the market," said one banker.
U.S. investors also liked Indian corporates.

"This is one country where the corporates are great -- but the government leaves something to be desired," said another. "If you had 10 issues from India (in the U.S. market), they would all get picked up," a fixed-income analyst said.
In other news, bankers expect several Korean banks to issue U.S. dollars in the form of floating-rate notes (FRNs).
Kookmin Bank wants to raise up to US$200 million through an FRN from an MTN programme, and Korea International Merchant Bank may also raise US$50 million, bankers said.
Kookmin Bank is expected to issue a three-year structure with annual puts, because of investor reluctance to buy straight three-year debt without puts.
Bankers said Korea International Merchant Bank's issue would be for two years, and would feature an 18-month put.
Korea Exchange Bank may also issue FRNs, bankers said.
Malaysia's Ramatex Capital Ltd is in the market with a three-year FRN issued at 99.80 to float at 85 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
